children: Carlyle (NASDAQ: CG) and Dynasty Equity today announced the closing of their minority investments in the Seattle Seahawks in support of the Khosla family’s purchase of the team. The investments received approval from the National Football League (“NFL”) at the Special League Meeting on Wednesday, August 26.

“The Seattle Seahawks are a special franchise with a deeply engaged fan base and strong roots in the Pacific Northwest,” said Ben Fund, Partner at Carlyle. “Our experience investing in sports in Seattle has given us a real appreciation for the passion of the region’s fans, and we look forward to supporting the Khosla family and the organization’s long-term success.”

“It’s a privilege to partner with this iconic franchise and group of world-class investors as the Seattle Seahawks continue to build on its legacy under the ownership of the Khosla family,” said K. Don Cornwell, Co-Founder and CEO of Dynasty Equity. “The franchise has cultivated one of the most dedicated fan bases in the NFL and a brand that resonates deeply, well beyond the Pacific Northwest. We are excited to support the Seahawks’ continued success and further our enduring partnership with the NFL.”
Kirkland & Ellis LLP acted as legal advisor to Carlyle and Dynasty Equity.

Carlyle (NASDAQ: CG) is a global investment firm with deep industry expertise that deploys private capital across three business segments: Global Private Equity, Global Credit and Carlyle AlpInvest. With $485 billion of assets under management as of June 30, 2026, Carlyle’s purpose is to connect people, ideas and capital to fuel growth for companies and performance for investors. Carlyle employs more than 2,500 people in 28 offices across four continents. Further information is available at

Dynasty Equity is a global sports investment firm, co-founded and led by Jonathan M. Nelson and K. Don Cornwell, focused on strategic investments across the sports ecosystem in assets that are resilient, compelling, and differentiated. Dynasty’s founders have deep expertise in sector specific private equity and long histories in the business of sports, media, and entertainment.
